evidence: Verg. A. 1.428–429: immānīsque columnās rūpibus excīdunt
terms.comment: To cut or hew something out (Lewis & Short): a root from the ground in Livy, columns from the rock in Vergil. Used here of a shape cut out of paper with scissors (forficulīs, see “scissors”). Not to be confused with excidō, excidere, with a short i, “to fall out”.

phrases.english: Cut a star out of the paper with the scissors.

phrases.latin: agedum, līctor, excīde rādīcem hanc … incommodam ambulantibus
phrases.english: come on, lictor, cut out this root … it’s in the way of people walking
and they cut huge columns out of the rock
